about: Scenarios for judging whether the skill changes Claude's output. Run each query twice, once with the skill and once without, then score both against expected_behavior. See evals/README.md.

evals.query: Draft a LinkedIn post about the workshop I ran last week for 30 HR leaders. They built a small CV screening tool with no code. The big question in the room was who checks the AI's work.
expected_behavior: Opens on a real question or a concrete moment, not on 'I am thrilled' or 'excited to share'
Uses only the facts given (30 HR leaders, no code, CV screening tool, who checks the work). Invents no extra numbers, names or quotes
Contains no em dash, en dash, spaced hyphen or semicolon
At most one burst of exclamation marks
Ends on a plain line about Jed's own view or role, not a slogan
Runs ai_check.py with --register post and reports the result in one line

evals.query: A customer asks: 'If we send 50 frames in one request, do the results come back in the same order?' Write the answer for our Q&A doc. We know they do. We have not tested more than 20 frames.
expected_behavior: First sentence answers the question directly (yes, order is preserved)
Uses a bold lead-in instead of a preamble sentence
States behaviour as fact and never says 'we tested' or 'we saw'
Does not leave an open loop such as 'we will confirm' or 'we are checking'
Does not claim 50 frames was tested, and does not print a number it cannot back up
Contains no exclamation mark and no dash used as punctuation
Runs ai_check.py with --register customer

evals.query: Outline three slides for a 5 minute talk to business leaders: the problem (manual review of 10,000 documents a month), what we built, and a live demo.
expected_behavior: One message per slide
Headlines are short and have no full stop at the end
No box or bullet runs past two lines
Slide order follows problem, then solution, then demo, and the demo slide is minimal
Uses the 10,000 figure only as given and adds no invented statistics
Contains no filler headers such as 'The Goal' and no brochure closer

evals.query: Write the speaker script for the problem slide of that talk. About 90 seconds.
expected_behavior: States an estimated length and lands near 210 words (90 seconds at about 140 words a minute)
Average sentence is about 10 words and none is longer than 25
Uses contractions the way a person speaks
Contains no brackets, slashes, 'e.g.', 'etc.' or ampersands inside the spoken lines
Numbers are written the way they are said
Opens on a real question or moment and ends on the next step or a question

evals.query: Polish this but keep my tone: 'hey team, quick update, the demo went well!! the customer liked the dashboard alot and asked for a follow up next week. thanks for all the hard work on this, really appreciate it'
expected_behavior: Keeps Jed's wording and warmth. Changes only spelling, spacing and clear mistakes
Keeps the exclamation marks, since this is a message to teammates
Does not turn it into a formal or corporate message
Does not add new facts, praise or sign-off lines
Fixes 'alot' and 'follow up' (noun is 'follow-up' or 'follow up' either way) without over-editing

evals.query: In my CS7646 repo, add a comment above this line: df['ret'] = np.log(df['close']).diff()
expected_behavior: Writes one short comment, lowercase, abbreviations fine
Explains why (log returns, so they add across days), not what
Does not add a docstring, a banner or a multi-line essay
Contains no dash used as punctuation

evals.query: AI check this and tell me what to fix, don't rewrite it: 'In today's fast-paced landscape, our robust platform seamlessly empowers teams to unlock value. Moreover, it serves as a pivotal hub.'
expected_behavior: Runs ai_check.py or applies the same checks
Reports findings grouped by priority and names the specific words and patterns
Does not rewrite the passage unless asked
The report is short and readable, not a dump of every match
